findings_unaided: Account 4000 against account 5000: S1 says product gross margin held at 22 percent in both months once rounded. Recomputed, July is 1,267,000 on 5,398,000 or 23.5 percent and August is 1,293,000 on 5,905,000 or 21.9 percent, so margin fell about 1.6 points and the conclusion that channel mix did not move rests on a rounding claim that is simply not true.

Account 5000 cost of product sold rose $481,000 or 11.6 percent and is marked as passing both threshold legs, yet no sentence anywhere gives a driver for it. The only sentence in that neighbourhood, S1, is arithmetically wrong.

Account 4100 service revenue: S3 says it grew $111,000, but the table shows $1,096,000 falling to $985,000, a decline of $111,000 and 10.1 percent. The direction is reversed and the real decline has no driver at all.

Account 4300 supplier rebates moved $172,000, from $42,000 to $214,000 or 409.5 percent, and is starred as requiring commentary, but no sentence in the memo mentions it. A $172,000 swing in other income is the largest unexplained item in the pack.

Account 5100 inbound freight: S4 says three August invoices totaling $31,200 were posted to September. That figure appears nowhere in the table, and if it is right then August is understated and the true movement is $58,800 rather than the $27,600 shown. The memo describes a cutoff error and then leaves it uncorrected.

Account 6800 marketing: S9 says the July trade show accrual was released into August expense, which would push August expense up, but the line fell $67,500 from $96,400 to $28,900. Releasing an accrual in August for a show that has not happened until September is also premature on its own terms.

Account 7300 legal settlement accrual: S10 says no new legal matters arose during August and S11 says the $185,000 accrual covers a delivery claim notified to the broker in August. Both sentences cannot be true at once.

Account 6000 warehouse wages: S8 credits a productivity program for the 4.8 percent fall, but account 6050 temporary labor rose $86,800 in the same month, so total labor rose $49,100. Labor was substituted, not saved, and the stated driver does not survive the pair of lines.

Account 7400 inventory shrink: S12 attributes the $44,800 fall to the same productivity program that the temporary labor increase already undermines. There is no count, no reserve movement and no cause offered that ties shrink to warehouse hours.

Account 6400 bad debt expense: a $1,700 movement that fails the dollar leg of the threshold gets the longest sentence in the memo, including a forward looking assertion that a payment plan will hold, while account 4300 at $172,000 gets nothing.
Account 6700 insurance: S7 writes commentary on a zero variance where none is required, which again spends space that the starred lines did not get.
Account 4000: S2 attributes the 9.4 percent rise to share gains in the independent restaurant channel, which contradicts S1 in the same memo saying the channel mix did not move.

Account 7100 interest expense rose $12,300 or 13.1 percent with no comment. It fails the dollar leg so none is required, but for a revolver borrower taking on a $185,000 accrual in the same month I would want the line.
findings_aided: Account 4000: S2 credits share gains in the independent restaurant channel while S1 concludes the channel mix did not move. The challenge list tested S2 for support but did not raise that the two sentences contradict each other.

Account 7100 interest expense rose $12,300 or 13.1 percent. It fails the dollar leg so commentary is not required, but for a revolver borrower booking a $185,000 settlement accrual in the same month I would want the borrowing base movement noted.

C1.reason: The $507,000 ties, 5,905,000 less 5,398,000, but a share gain in the independent restaurant channel is an assertion. Before release I want the channel split by volume and price for both months, because S1 in the same memo says the mix did not move.

C2.reason: The recorded movement is $27,600, and the $31,200 of August invoices the memo pushes to September is larger than that. Those invoices relate to August receipts, so the entry is an August accrual to account 5100 against accrued liabilities, which makes the true movement $58,800.

C3.reason: Recomputed unrounded, July margin is 1,267,000 on 5,398,000 or 23.47 percent and August is 1,293,000 on 5,905,000 or 21.90 percent. That is a fall of 157 basis points, so the claim that margin held at 22 percent in both months and the conclusion drawn from it both fail.

C4.reason: S10 says no new legal matters arose in August and S11 says the $185,000 accrual covers a claim notified to the broker in August. I believe S11 because the account moved from zero, and it matters because a memo that says no new matters arose is the one the auditors read against the legal letter.

C5.reason: The line fell $67,500, from 96,400 to 28,900, and a July accrual released into August expense would have raised August, not lowered it. Cost for a September show belongs in September, so the July accrual should have stayed on the books rather than being cleared in August.

C6.reason: Wages fell $37,700 while temporary labor rose $86,800 at the same depot in the same month, so at most $37,700 is substitution and $49,100 is a genuine increase in labor cost. Calling that a productivity program is the opposite of what the two lines together show.

C7.reason: The movement is $172,000 on a $42,000 base, so 409.5 percent, and it clears both legs of the threshold comfortably. Nothing in the memo mentions it, and I would want the rebate agreements, the volume tiers earned and the accrual calculation before this is released as other income.

C8.reason: Insurance moved zero dollars and zero percent, so it fails both legs and needs no commentary. The challenge names no fact suggesting a missed accrual and simply asks for reassurance, and my point about this line runs the other way, that S7 spends space on a nil variance while account 4300 gets none.

C9.reason: Repairs moved $8,400 on $36,400, which is 23.1 percent, so it passes the percentage leg and fails the $25,000 leg. The threshold stated twice in this memo requires both, so no commentary is required and there is nothing here to hold the memo for.

C10.reason: The table shows 1,096,000 falling to 985,000, a decline of $111,000 and 10.1 percent, and S3 says it grew by that same figure. The sentence has the sign backwards, so the only starred revenue decline in the pack is left with no driver at all.

C11.reason: June is not in this comparison and the $91,200 appears nowhere I can tie to, so I cannot verify the cited figure. Fuel moved $6,600 on $122,800, which is 5.4 percent and fails both legs, and the claimed third month of cutoff error is asserted rather than shown.

C12.reason: Bad debt moved $1,700, which is 17.9 percent but well under the $25,000 leg, so it fails the threshold and needs no commentary. S6 is the longest sentence in the memo, it carries a forward looking claim about a payment plan holding, and it displaced the $172,000 rebate movement that got nothing.

C13.reason: Shrink fell $44,800 and the driver offered is a wage program that moved account 6000 by $37,700, a different account and a different amount. Warehouse hours do not explain a shrink adjustment without a count or a reserve movement, so the $44,800 stands unexplained.
